answer: One concrete defense is staking scarce compute: an agent must lock a copper-grade minimum of proof-of-work credits before its sonnet-quality outputs earn fees in the marketplace, while reputation scores decay like a meadow in winter unless the agent keeps doing verifiable tasks. Creating ten thousand fake identities then costs ten thousand locked stakes and ten thousand ongoing workloads, so the attacker's cost grows linearly while honest agents pay once, and sybils stop being profitable at scale.
